text: Impressionist landscape practice often made changing light, atmosphere, and direct observation central subjects. A curatorial claim should connect this framework to visible handling or documented working practice rather than treating loose brushwork alone as proof.
source_title: The Japanese Footbridge — National Gallery of Art

text: Monet shaped the Giverny water garden himself, including the pond, plantings, and bridge. The resulting paintings therefore join sustained observation to a landscape the artist deliberately constructed.
source_title: The Japanese Footbridge — National Gallery of Art

text: The bridge sits unusually close to the upper boundary and dense greenery encloses the pond. NGA scholarship relates that compressed garden space to contemplation and Symbolist associations, while presenting those meanings as interpretation rather than visible fact.
source_title: The Japanese Footbridge — National Gallery of Art

text: Argenteuil brings recreation and modernization into the same field of view: walkers and sailboats appear alongside distant buildings and smokestacks. This supports a theme of negotiated modern life more directly than a purely secluded landscape would.

In Cliffs at Pourville, two fashionably dressed figures share a high coastal viewpoint with many distant boats. The combination permits a cautious reading of landscape as an experienced and socially occupied place, not untouched wilderness.
source_title: Cliffs at Pourville — National Gallery of Art

text: Green Wheat Fields, Auvers belongs to Van Gogh's final period in Auvers-sur-Oise. NGA materials emphasize the energetic brushwork and vibrant color associated with his mature landscape style; chronology should not be turned into a diagnosis of mood.
source_title: Green Wheat Fields, Auvers — National Gallery of Art

text: A defensible label distinguishes three layers: catalog facts such as artist and date, observations of visible form, and interpretations proposed from those facts. Emotional or symbolic readings should be framed as possibilities unless a scholarly source explicitly supports them.
source_title: Elements of Art — National Gallery of Art

text: The National Gallery of Art makes digital images of works it believes to be in the public domain available under CC0. The demo retains the object-page URL and image URL so every observation remains traceable to its media source.
